{"id":"mimid-604m.6","title":"host_room commits 28 times for one room, under the agent mutex","description":"The dominant hop of a first private message (bead mimid-604m.2: 78% of
the action, 429.7 ms idle and 21.2 s under I/O pressure) is
Store::open_direct -> Agent::host_room + Agent::invite, and it holds the
agent mutex throughout.

Counted here with SQLite's file change counter on the agent's own
database, around each call, in a worktree at da3f1555:

  Agent::host_room   28 write transactions
  Agent::invite       2 write transactions

28 of the sender's 36 transactions for one first private message are
host_room, and at four fsyncs a commit they are 112 of its 145 fsyncs.
They are not MLS steps that a crash needs to tell apart: they are
OpenMLS's own writes while a new group is built, each its own
transaction because nothing had a transaction open. Agent::build_commit,
Agent::join and Agent::join_external all wrap the same kind of work in
Agent::in_transaction; host_room was the one path that did not.

## What this does

Puts Member::create, the first Commit, the merge and the ratchet tree in
one Agent::in_transaction, which closes before Room/create. host_room
then commits 4 times, not 28.

## The mutex

Store::host must hold the agent across host_room and every invite, and
this does not change that. Store::sync's reconcile_rooms makes a record
for any room the agent is active in that the store has no record of, so
a window between host_room and invite would give one room two records
under two keys; and when an invite fails, Store::host leaves the room
again and tells the caller no room was made, which a record the sync had
already made would contradict. The critical section is right; its length
was not.","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-28T02:03:25.002806931Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-28T02:03:25.002806931Z","dependencies":[{"issue_id":"mimid-604m.6","depends_on_id":"mimid-604m","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-11-28T02:03:25.052786126Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"}]}
